plain: n8n connects nodes that receive, transform and send data. Start with an offline logic lab, then configure the trigger, credentials and destination. Importing a workflow does not connect accounts or prove that external actions succeeded. The expanded project workbooks and downloadable training materials are currently in Spanish.

account.free: Use n8n Cloud or a maintained self-hosted installation. Check current pricing and limits before choosing. Hosting resources are finite, and external APIs may charge separately.
steps: Create a workflow in an instance you can access. Record its version and use fictional data.
Use the workflow menu to import the downloaded JSON file. Inspect its manual trigger, sample, transformation and assertion nodes.
Execute manually. The assertion must return passed:true. Change an expected value in a copy to check that a mismatch causes failure.
Follow the workbook to map actual input fields, select test credentials and inspect the destination response.
Check errors and repeated inputs. Publish the reviewed workflow, use the production webhook URL and inspect executions.
account.warning: The lab tests local logic. External connections require their own configuration and verification.

first: Import a lab from its JSON file.
Read its sample and explain the required fields.
Execute and compare expected with result.
Keep the original and test the specified variation.
Follow the implementation guide to connect services.
shortcuts: Use the workflow menu and inspect the imported nodes.
Inspect the resolved value and type of each mapped field.
Review the executions retained by your instance configuration.
daily: Keep destination confirmations and reconcile uncertain results.
errors: Check method and URL. Test URLs require listening; production URLs require a published workflow.
Inspect the actual input and referenced node. Webhook payload fields usually appear inside body.
Check credential validity, permissions and the requested resource.
Check provider limits and Retry-After. Use bounded retries and reconcile external effects.
Use persistent identity and a unique constraint; an in-memory Set only covers the current calculation.
words: Node
Each box on the board. A box is an app doing one thing: 'Gmail sending an email', 'OpenAI writing text'. Add them with the Tab key and open them with a double-click.
Canvas
The gray board where you place boxes and connect them with lines. You move around it by dragging with Ctrl held down, and you fit everything on screen with the 1 key.
Trigger
The first box, the one that decides when everything starts. It has a rounded corner and a lightning bolt. Without a real trigger, n8n won't let you activate the flow.
Execution
One complete pass of the flow, from the first box to the last, whether it has three steps or forty. It's the unit n8n charges you by, which is why it comes out much cheaper than Zapier on long flows.
Item

Each individual piece of data traveling through the pipe. If the first node brings in 20 emails, that's 20 items, and the next nodes run 20 times, once for each. Understanding this avoids 90% of surprises.
Expression
A formula between double curly braces, {{ }}, that gets replaced with real data when it runs. It writes itself when you drag a field from the INPUT column. The field turns purple when it holds one.
Data pin
The pin, P key. Freezes a test's result so that node always returns the same thing while you're building. It only works while testing by hand: once the flow is active, the pin is ignored.
Credential
The saved permission you give n8n to access your Gmail, your Telegram, or your OpenAI account. It lives outside the flows, under 'Overview' > 'Credentials', and every node for that app shares it.
Webhook

A web address n8n gives you so something else can notify it. Your vibe-coded website calls that address when someone makes a purchase, and n8n kicks in. It has two versions, test and production, and mixing them up is the most common mistake.
Self-hosted
Running n8n on a rented computer of your own instead of theirs. It costs about $4-6 a month with unlimited executions, but updates, backups, and outages are your responsibility.
ignore: Adding AI when a visible rule is sufficient.
